clue.text: Tom maybe goes around bald for show

indicators.note: the tomcat's letters surround the next piece, as if walking round it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, given as one example by 'maybe'
bald means bare, without hair

explanation.surface: A tomcat sidesteps a bald patch for the sake of appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment, a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Athens is splendid!

definitions.meaning: the chief city of Greece and its seat of government

explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, and 'capital!' is a dated cry meaning excellent.

clue.text: A couple of places for drinking in without a hooligan to be seen

indicators.note: two copies of the drinking place are needed, a couple meaning a pair

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word in surrounds the letter a

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thug spotted in two pubs, or left outside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: IN goes round A to give IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is an uncivilised, brutish person, much like a lout.

clue.text: Bird that's about late in the day

parts.note: re means about or concerning
eve is evening, the late part of the day

explanation.surface: A bird known for being out late in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: The person taking part ending disastrously

definitions.text: The person taking part ending disastrously

parts.words: The person taking part ending disastrously
parts.note: reads as someone whose role went wrong, but means an actor playing a role in a drama that ends in catastrophe

explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor in tragedies, plays whose endings bring ruin.

clue.text: Tell some soldiers to number

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to number is to count

explanation.surface: An order to tell a few soldiers to count off.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to narrate or relate, as in telling a story.

clue.text: Some men on the board may be cheats

definitions.meaning: chess pieces, the castles of the board

explanation.definitionFit: Rooks are chess pieces, and to rook someone is to swindle them, so rooks are also swindlers.

clue.text: A singer joking with popular companion

parts.note: chaff is light-hearted teasing banter
in means fashionable, popular
CH, Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A vocalist trading banter with a well-liked friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European songbird.

clue.text: French article no-one read up, causing joint concern

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up means reading backwards

parts.note: no and one, with one given as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece that nobody bothered to read, causing worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read up' turns NO I into ION, since down clues read upwards backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is an organisation formed for joint purposes, a combined enterprise.

clue.text: "X" sets out, though most nervous

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of sets are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone marked X sets off, though very anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SETS to SEST; X is Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means anxious and on edge; the superlative is the most strained.

clue.text: Coppers press for a clean-up campaign

parts.note: P stands for pence, the copper coins of British money
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Police officers push hard for a drive against crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but it means copper coins, pence, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is a sweeping removal of unwanted people, a political clearing-out drive.

clue.text: Commercial address gaining esteem

parts.note: a commercial on television is an advert, an ad
an address is a formal speech, an oration

explanation.surface: A business speech wins respect from its listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and reverence, an intense form of high regard.

clue.text: Awful scare lest solution can't be found

indicators.note: an awful version of these words is a mangled one, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful fright that a solver's answer may be lost forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges SCARE LEST; 'solution' only joins, hinting at the solved letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traceless leaves no sign behind, so it cannot be located.

clue.text: Law-breaker pales

definitions.meaning: a receiver who deals in stolen goods, a criminal
pales are wooden stakes, and a row of them forms a barrier

explanation.definitionFit: A fence is slang for a handler of stolen property, and also a barrier built of upright posts.

clue.text: Scottish VIP prepared to receive the monarch

indicators.note: the first word takes the monarch's letter inside itself, receiving it

parts.note: a table laid is a table prepared
R for Rex or Regina, the reigning king or queen

explanation.surface: A Scottish dignitary gets ready to welcome the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner, a person of local standing and importance.

clue.text: Put off vulgar male cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
gent is a colloquial, somewhat common, word for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Discouraging a crude man who works as a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleansing agent, something used for washing.

clue.text: Manager getting mean with a worker

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A boss becomes stingy with an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like 'stingy' but is the verb 'intend'.
explanation.definitionFit: An intendant is an administrator or superintendent, especially of an opera house.

clue.text: Dealing with those having some complaint?

definitions.text: Dealing with those having some complaint?

parts.words: Dealing with those having some complaint?
parts.note: sounds like customer service handling grievances, but means medical care for patients with an illness

explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical care given to patients for an ailment, and generally the way one handles people.

clue.text: P.M. using No. Ten for a broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister uses Number Ten for a radio address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'P.M.' looks like the Prime Minister of Number Ten, but means post meridiem; 'broadcast' rearranges NO TEN FOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: p.m., post meridiem, marks the hours after noon.

clue.text: A girl has to study her position

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a stance is a stated position or posture

explanation.surface: A young woman must think carefully about where she stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female given name.

clue.text: A sailing ship — could be a cutter

explanation.definitionFit: A clipper is a fast sailing ship, and clippers are cutting tools for hair or nails.

clue.text: Tie is required, and that can be a problem

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a knot or loop
a snag or difficulty that holds things up

explanation.surface: A tie is needed, and that may cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is both a knot used to fasten a rope and a minor setback.

clue.text: Love taking pupils in hand in the country

indicators.note: the love and pupils letters go inside the word hand

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
L is a learner, so two of them are LL

explanation.surface: Love that guides students by the hand in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O and LL inside HAND; L is a learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland is a common name for the Netherlands.

clue.text: Put down in plain terms

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words plain terms, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Written down in simple language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in plain terms' sounds like 'simply put', but 'in' marks the letters inside PLAIN TERMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting a body down into the ground.

clue.text: Quickly moves rubbish in back street

indicators.note: the rubbish goes inside the turned-round street abbreviation
back turns the street abbreviation backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Garbage hurries along a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST to TS, and 'in' puts ROT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to go at a brisk pace, between walking and running.

clue.text: College the artist left after he'd found the church

indicators.note: the artist and left come after the letters of he'd in the answer

parts.note: CAT was a College of Advanced Technology, a type of British college of the 1960s
he'd taken as written, without its apostrophe
RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist quits college once he has discovered religion.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT stood for a College of Advanced Technology, a British type of college now gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Reason for suit having superior lining

indicators.note: the superior letter lines the inside of the suit word

parts.note: a lawsuit is a case in court
U means upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: Why a suit has a fancy lining.
explanation.walkthrough: U, for upper-class, is a British convention for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause is a reason or motive for something.

clue.text: Slippery customer, always without cash

indicators.note: without means outside, so always surrounds the cash letter

parts.note: ever means always
L is the pound sign, standing for money

explanation.surface: A shifty character, forever broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: EVER goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a famously slippery creature.

clue.text: Prefer charges cut, so peer made out

indicators.note: the letters of these words are made out into a new order, worked into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A nobleman's reduced fees lead him to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer charges is to bring them formally, which is what bringing a case to court means.

clue.text: She's played in an orchestra

parts.note: reads like a female musician, but the 'she' is a girl's name that is also a stringed instrument bowed in orchestras

explanation.definitionFit: Viola is a woman's name, from Twelfth Night, and a string instrument a little larger than a violin.

clue.text: Odd trees to favour!

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of trees and to are set out strangely, in a new order

explanation.surface: A strange thing for trees to be preferred!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges TREES TO; 'favour' is a noun, a badge worn as a token.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon or badge worn to show support, like a rosette pinned on.

clue.text: Exalted, having quickly finished with Edward

parts.note: finished means through, written quickly in its short form thro
Ned is a familiar form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Raised up after speedily finishing with Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: THRO is the shortened spelling of 'through', meaning finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Throned means seated on a throne, raised to royal dignity.
